name: Chicken 65 Totopos
indian_anchor: South Indian Chicken 65: small boneless thigh pieces, dry to lightly coated, deep red-orange, curry leaf and green chile (Chennai-associated; origin contested, V-61)
mexican_anchor: Fried nixtamal corn totopos as the chip/base (totopos names the chip; NASHA's thick fried chip is a design choice, not a Mexican standard, V-63)
nasha_transformation: The chip becomes the plate: chicken and chip are built to be eaten together; crema (not raita) as optional cooling; lime and onion default
cultural_class: MODERN FUSION overall; Chicken 65 = CULTURALLY INSPIRED; thick fried chip = ORIGINAL HOUSE COMPOSITION; Hyderabad/Andhra lineage = UNCERTAIN/ADVISOR
core_ingredients: boneless chicken thigh; yogurt-ginger-garlic-lemon marinade; rice flour + cornflour coating; curry leaf; green chile; fried corn tortilla wedges; crema; lime; onion
proposed_construction: THREE constructions under test: A Integrated, B Ring, C Composed board (sheet 11); bare-chip control
cooking_method: Marinate, coat just before frying, fry at about 175 C in small batches, probe to 74 C; chips fried last
equipment: fryer (H load), probe thermometer, rack, hot hold 90 C
texture_target: Crisp-shell juicy chicken; chip still crisp at T+10 (gate 3.5)
acid: lemon in marinade, lime at service
garnish_purpose: fried curry leaf and chile = Chicken 65 identity cue; lime/onion = acid and freshness
service_vessel: board or plate; crema on the side or integrated per construction
holding_risk: HIGH: moisture migration into chip; 10-minute failure gate
execution_risk: medium: fryer pressure, second person, oil handling
d54_risk: low: chicken only; no lard in tortillas or oil
allergens_proposed: milk (yogurt, crema); possible egg if cook adds it; wheat NOT expected (rice flour/cornflour) but cross-contact in fryer to be recorded; no allergen-free claim
reference_gaps: Chennai dry-vs-sauced original unconfirmed; thick-chip fry data from industrial patents only; no controlled study of chip under hot protein (L-001..L-005)
next_experiment: Session 1 exactly as frozen (sheet 13 shopping list and cook card)
confidence: medium for the concept; none for any result

name: Paneer Tikka Taco
indian_anchor: Paneer tikka: thick spiced hung-curd marinade, char, soft paneer, onion/capsicum; North Indian/Punjabi restaurant tradition (no documented inventor)
mexican_anchor: Corn-tortilla taco with green salsa, raw onion, cilantro, lime; charred-meat-taco (al carbon) is inspiration only and unsourced
nasha_transformation: Tandoor-style char on a taco; acid and salsa architecture does what raita/chutney does; optional charred pineapple (never called al pastor)
cultural_class: MODERN FUSION; paneer tikka = CULTURALLY INSPIRED; taco form = CULTURALLY INSPIRED; pineapple = UNCERTAIN/ADVISOR (al pastor echo)
core_ingredients: paneer (about 2 cm cubes); hung curd, ginger-garlic, chile, kasuri methi, chaat masala, neutral oil (mustard oil EXCLUDED from the baseline, V-72), optional besan/ajwain; corn tortilla 12-15 cm; salsa verde; onion; cilantro; lime
proposed_construction: 3-4 cubes per taco (about 45-70 g paneer, TEST START), onion/capsicum 10-15 g, salsa 10-15 g; two small tacos per order
cooking_method: Marinate 1-4 h; char over very high heat to order (tandoor if available; else charbroiler/comal/oven+broiler as labelled substitute)
equipment: tandoor (unresolved) or charbroiler/comal; comal for tortillas
texture_target: Soft interior, visible char, crust that clings; tortilla does not tear
acid: lime, salsa verde, pickled red onion
garnish_purpose: salsa and onion supply the Mexican identity and the acid that cuts paneer richness
service_vessel: two tacos on a plate, salsa on the side
holding_risk: MEDIUM-HIGH: paneer firms and dries, tortilla steams; finish to order
execution_risk: medium: depends on the unresolved tandoor/hood answer
d54_risk: low: paneer; check rennet source/animal rennet only matters for vegetarian claims, not D-54
allergens_proposed: milk (paneer, yogurt); mustard only if mustard oil or a mustard blend is ever used (excluded from baseline); wheat only if flour tortilla; no allergen-free claim
reference_gaps: no professional-kitchen source (home blogs only, T1); cube size and heat source disagree across sources; Session 2 thresholds are AGENT-PROPOSED in food/sessions/sessions.json (D-76) and need founder confirmation before cooking; mustard oil: in the US it is commonly sold labelled for external use only, so its legal status as a food ingredient must be confirmed before it goes in a marinade (T4, unverified; a substitute oil is an option)
next_experiment: Session 2: ONE variable = heat source; marinade, cut, tortilla constant; hold at 0/5/10 min

name: Goat Birria, Sealed-Pot Braise
indian_anchor: Dum-style sealed-pot braise; whole-spice toasting; bhuna-style frying of the adobo paste (technique only)
mexican_anchor: Jalisco birria de chivo: bone-in goat in guajillo-ancho adobo with vinegar and spices, braised, with consomme; corn tortillas, onion, cilantro, lime, salsa
nasha_transformation: Keeps goat/adobo/consomme identity; Indian layer limited to technique that improves depth; yogurt-papaya marinade and curry-leaf tadka are TESTED AGAINST a plain adobo control, not assumed
cultural_class: Goat, adobo, consomme, tortilla/onion/cilantro/lime = HISTORICALLY SUPPORTED (T1, advisor to confirm); dipped griddled taco = MODERN FUSION/adaptation (Tijuana/LA, typically beef); sealed pot = CULTURALLY INSPIRED parallel; bhuna adobo = ORIGINAL HOUSE COMPOSITION; yogurt-papaya and curry leaf = UNCERTAIN/ADVISOR
core_ingredients: bone-in goat shoulder/leg; guajillo and ancho adobo (vinegar, Mexican oregano, cumin, cinnamon, clove, bay); goat/chicken/vegetable stock only; corn tortillas; onion; cilantro; lime; salsa
proposed_construction: Goat taco(s) with consomme in a small cup; NO cheese by default; bones and visible fibre kept so it reads as goat, not beef
cooking_method: Sear, bhuna the adobo paste, seal, low braise; skim; dip tortillas in surface fat and griddle
equipment: oven or kettle (long braise), comal/griddle, cold storage, hot hold
texture_target: Tender but fibrous goat; drinkable consomme; tortilla holds after dipping
garnish_purpose: raw onion, cilantro, lime cut the fat and mark it as Mexican
service_vessel: small clay or steel cup for consomme (katori-like), tacos on a plate
holding_risk: HIGH: large braise cooling/reheating/hold, fat set in consomme (food-safety professional must set the process)
execution_risk: HIGH: long lead, sourcing, yield and trim waste unknown
d54_risk: MEDIUM: stock and bones must be goat/chicken/vegetable only; no beef stock/bone, no pork lard in tortillas; not halal, no halal claim
allergens_proposed: milk if yogurt marinade; possible wheat if seal dough; celery/others per stock; no allergen-free claim
reference_gaps: goat age/cut standard NOT FOUND; no authoritative braise temperature; Mexican advisor review; cold-chain and reheating rules not researched
next_experiment: Small pilot per the Session 5 card (about 3 kg bone-in): plain adobo vs adobo+Indian layer (one variable), record yield, trim, skim, 60/120 min hold; blind vs lamb taco

name: Butter Chicken & Roasted Poblano Quesadilla
indian_anchor: Murgh makhani: tomato-butter-cream gravy, kasuri methi, charred tandoori-style chicken (origin contested in court, do not pick one)
mexican_anchor: Quesadilla con rajas: roasted poblano strips, melting cheese (Oaxaca-style), griddled on a comal
nasha_transformation: Reduced clingy makhani and charred chicken pieces inside a griddled quesadilla; poblano smoke and acid cut the richness; dip optional and separate
cultural_class: MODERN FUSION; butter chicken = CULTURALLY INSPIRED; quesadilla con rajas = CULTURALLY INSPIRED; dip = ORIGINAL HOUSE COMPOSITION
core_ingredients: chicken thigh (about 1 cm dice, tandoori-style char); reduced makhani; roasted poblano rajas (drained); Oaxaca-style cheese (record rennet source); flour or corn tortilla (open)
proposed_construction: 25 cm tortilla folded: cheese against both faces as barrier, sauced filling in the centre, rajas against the cheese; TEST START about 40-50 g cheese, 50-70 g chicken-sauce, 20-30 g rajas
cooking_method: Reduce sauce and chill filling; dry comal, medium heat, light press; rest 1-2 min before cutting
equipment: comal/flat-top (H load), tandoor optional for chicken, oven/grill alternative
texture_target: Crisp-browned tortilla, set filling, melted cheese fused, no leak
freshness: low (needs the poblano and a fresh garnish)
garnish_purpose: rajas and an acid/fresh garnish are the counterweight to richness
service_vessel: cut wedges showing cross-section; dip in a cup
holding_risk: MEDIUM: steams soft if covered; filling leaks if sauce not reduced
execution_risk: medium-high: comal is the shared bottleneck
allergens_proposed: milk (butter, cream, cheese, yogurt); wheat if flour tortilla; tree nut only if cashew in the gravy (default cashew-free); no allergen-free claim
reference_gaps: sauce-colour reference low authority; 'Raita-crema' vs butter-chicken dip disagree between sheet and library; leak/sog limit blank in sheet 05
next_experiment: Session 4: sauce thickness first (spoon-coat/reduction time vs leak minutes); then cheese barrier; then chicken size
